ruling.recommended_action: Send the case file to a human safety reviewer: attach the rider's complaint (speeding, hard braking, shoulder overtaking, "scared and felt unsafe"), the complete timestamped chat (F3–F5), the driver's post-trip statement (F6), the trip record (F1, F2) and both profiles (F7, F8); note that no speed/harsh-braking telemetry or in-trip call recording exists, and take no interim measure on the record as it stands.
ruling.reasoning:
The screen is run first, on every case, whatever type was filed. The rider's filed complaint states that the driver was "speeding and braking hard the whole way, overtaking on the shoulder" and that the rider "was scared and felt unsafe" [F1][F2]. That is a dangerous-driving allegation plus a statement of feeling unsafe, so the safety screen engages under SAFE-1 and SAFE-2, and the trace confirms this: SAFE-1 is ✓ with escalate the only allowed outcome.

Reading the rest of the record for safety content: the two chat messages are ordinary — the rider's pickup note "I'm at the taxi stand outside the MRT already, in a red cap" [F3] and the driver's "2 min away, blue Toyota Prius" [F4], both timestamped [F5]. Neither contains a threat, insult, harassment or inappropriate conduct, and the driver's written statement "I drove normally. The rider was on the phone the whole trip and never complained to me" [F6] is a denial, not an aggravating remark. The screen therefore finds no separate abuse or threat; the safety content is the alleged dangerous driving itself, which is enough for escalation under SAFE-1 / SAFE-2.

Because the dispute is a safety case, SAFE-3 applies: the system may gather evidence, summarise accounts and prepare the file, but it may not rule, assign fault or recommend an outcome. So I make no finding on whether the driving was dangerous and express no view on either account's credibility — the rider's complaint of dangerous driving and fear and the driver's denial are precisely what the human reviewer must weigh.

What the record holds for the reviewer: the trip ran 8.3 km against an 8.4 km optimal route, i.e. 0.1 km under, inside the 1 km tolerance of RD-1, so there is no excess distance and no off-route segment to refund under RD-2 [F1]. Duration was 8.2 min against a 13.8 min estimate, 5.6 min shorter; that is a duration record only, and the file contains no speed, acceleration or harsh-braking telemetry and no in-trip call recording, so it neither proves nor disproves "speeding" or "overtaking on the shoulder" — a point both advocates accept (C5, D4, D5). The allegations rest on the rider's complaint [F1] against the driver's post-trip statement [F6]; per TH-3 those accounts conflict and credibility is a matter for a person, not for this court.

Profiles are considered but decide nothing: rider 1187 days, rating 4.6, 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days [F7]; driver 675 days, rating 4.85, 963 trips in 90 days, 0 disputes and 0 upheld [F8]. Neither profile supports an account flag under RD-6 or an interim measure under SAFE-4, and per SAFE-3 I recommend no such measure — the escalation itself is the outcome.

Both advocates asked only for escalation and expressly disclaimed any refund (C2, D7, rebuttals), so no amount is set here; under SAFE-3 no outcome beyond the file is mine to recommend. Best fit precedent is not invoked because a safety incident is not decided by the route-deviation, surge or no-show precedents (DISP-2026-0089, -0142, -0211).
ruling.escalation_reason: Safety incident: the filed complaint alleges dangerous driving (speeding, hard braking, shoulder overtaking) and that the rider felt unsafe, which under SAFE-1 / SAFE-2 goes to a human reviewer; SAFE-3 bars the AI from ruling, assigning fault or recommending an outcome. The record is complete for the file (timestamped chat F3–F5, driver statement F6, trip data F1–F2, profiles F7–F8) but no speed or braking telemetry exists, so the conflicting accounts must be weighed by a person.

rejected_claims.reason: Not rejected as a basis for escalation — the complaint is a dangerous-driving allegation and the escalation follows [F1][SAFE-1][SAFE-2]; but to the extent it asserts the allegation is established, no finding of fault can be made [SAFE-3].
Accepted: safety path is escalation only, the system may prepare the file but not rule or assign fault [F5][SAFE-1][SAFE-3] — this is the ruling, not a finding for either side.

Its premise that the safety allegation rests only on the filed complaint and is for a human is correct [F3][F4][F5][SAFE-1], but the inference that the complete silent chat weighs either way is not a finding this court can make; credibility is for the reviewer [TH-3].
Accepted as to escalation: the accounts conflict, the driver's statement is his own claim [F6], and SAFE-3 bars a system finding on fault — a summary, not an outcome, is prepared.

Rejected: the F2 duration record (8.2 min against 13.8 min) is a duration measurement only and carries no speed or braking data, so it cannot be read as corroborating 'speeding' or shoulder overtaking [F1][F2][SAFE-1]; the driver's rival reading (D4) is equally unavailable.
Accepted: neither profile decides the case [F7][F8] and no flag or interim measure is supported [RD-6][SAFE-4]; the review turns on the complaint and the trip record.
Accepted: dangerous-driving allegation → human review, system barred from ruling or assigning fault [F5][SAFE-1][SAFE-2][SAFE-3].

Accepted that the chat contains no threat, harassment or inappropriate conduct by the driver [F4][F5][F6][SAFE-1]; that does not dispose of the dangerous-driving allegation raised in the complaint [F1]. No account flag is added.
Accepted: actual 8.3 km is 0.1 km under the 8.4 km optimal route, inside the 1 km tolerance, so no excess distance and nothing to refund [F1][RD-1][RD-2].
Accepted on its facts — no telemetry corroborates or refutes the manoeuvres [F2][SAFE-1][SAFE-3] — but it cannot be used to resolve the safety question either way; that is the reviewer's.

Rejected as a system finding: the pre-pickup chat [F3][F4] is neutral and the driver's post-trip statement [F6] is a claim, not a record; neither settles the conflicting accounts, so no credibility finding is made [TH-3] (and no RD-5 issue arises, as this is not a route-deviation case).
Accepted: profile history [F8][F7] gives no basis for a flag under RD-6 or an interim suspension under SAFE-4, and none is recommended [SAFE-3].
Accepted as withdrawn: no fare or excess-distance facts support any monetary refund and the rider has not asked for one; amount is null [F1][F2][RD-2].
